evals.prompt: Group the issues in the 0.22.2 milestone into sets I can each work on in a single PR.
evals.expected_output: Cohesive groups with files named, a merge order, and a parallelism verdict. #1932 and #2027 must be one group (adjacent arms of deepCopyValue's switch in src/gc_deep_copy.zig). #2129, #2194, #1982 and #2125 must be one group (all in src/primitives_srfi18.zig). #2127 must be identified as land-first because it is the detector for the rest.
expectations: #1932 and #2027 appear in the same group, justified by both being arms of the same switch in src/gc_deep_copy.zig
#2129, #2194, #1982 and #2125 appear in the same group, justified by all living in src/primitives_srfi18.zig
#2127 is ordered before the groups it verifies, on instrument-before-subject grounds
#1870 is ordered early on signal-before-work grounds (test-only, restores CI trust)
Every group names the files it touches
The response flags that src/primitives_srfi18.zig is near the 1500-line file-size cap and names a split seam
An explicit merge order is given, marking which groups are parallel

evals.prompt: Group the 0.22.3 milestone issues into single-PR sets.
evals.expected_output: Groups as above, plus #2043 reported as no longer reproducing (fixed by PR #2174 alongside its siblings #1893/#1920/#1940/#1945) and excluded from the groups rather than scheduled.
expectations: #2043 is reported as no-longer-reproducing and excluded from all groups
The report cites running the issue's own reproduction, not merely reading the body
#2043 is NOT closed without the user asking
#1930 and #2097 appear in the same group (both build-id staleness producing 'invalid embedded bytecode')
#1924 and #1933 are grouped separately from the local fixes and marked design-first
The long pole is named, with a statement of whether the rest ships without it

evals.prompt: Batch the open issues in milestone 9.9.9 into PRs.
evals.expected_output: A statement that no open issues carry that milestone, and no groups — must not fall back to the whole tracker.
expectations: Response states that the milestone matched no open issues
Response contains no groups
Response does not fall back to grouping all open issues

evals.prompt: Which of these can I do in one PR: 2044, 2085, 2179? (skill argument: 2044,2085,2179)
evals.expected_output: One group containing all three, justified as the zero-risk class — three independent .sld bugs touching no engine code — with a note that they are trivially splittable per-SRFI.
expectations: All three are placed in a single group
The justification is that all three are portable .sld fixes touching no Zig / engine code
The response notes they are trivially splittable if per-SRFI review is preferred
Each issue's library file is named (lib/srfi/146/hash.sld, lib/srfi/113.sld, lib/srfi/42.sld)

evals.prompt: I want to launch concurrent sessions on the 0.22.2 milestone rather than review a plan — give me the waves.
evals.expected_output: Bare paste-able wave lines containing only issue numbers, with every group in a wave touching files no other group in that wave touches.
expectations: Response contains 'Wave N:' lines with comma-separated issue numbers
No issue number appears in more than one wave
Groups sharing a file never appear in the same wave
The wave lines contain no prose or commands mixed in

evals.prompt: Start wave 1 sessions for the plan you just gave me.
evals.expected_output: One session per wave-1 group launched concurrently, each in its own git worktree on a branch off main, with a self-contained brief and the commit/PR wrap-up contract (regression test, DCO sign-off, per-issue Closes keyword).
expectations: Each group is launched in its own git worktree (Agent isolation: worktree, or git worktree add), never in the shared checkout or on main
Branches are cut from a freshly-fetched origin/main (git fetch first), not from the possibly-stale local checkout
All groups of the wave are launched concurrently rather than one at a time
Each session brief is self-contained and tells the session to read the issue bodies itself
The wrap-up contract is stated: regression test, git commit -s (DCO), push, gh pr create with a per-issue Closes line
Tests are directed to run in the foreground, not backgrounded waiting on a notification
The response does not treat a single worktree's green test run as proof that main is green
